steps.say: In term neonates, the tip of the spinal cord normally sits above the lower margin of the second lumbar vertebra. When the conus medullaris terminates at or below the third lumbar level, tethered cord syndrome must be suspected.
steps.tx: The **normal conus medullaris termination** lies above the lower border of **L2** in term neonates, ascending to the adult level at L1-L2 by 3 months of age. A conus ending at **L3 or lower** establishes a low-lying cord and signals pathologic mechanical tethering of neural elements.

vis.alt: Lumbosacral spine MRI showing conus medullaris termination and spinal cord.
vis.caption: Lumbosacral spine MRI: normal conus medullaris termination and thecal sac. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The filum terminale provides crucial diagnostic criteria on axial imaging. A filum diameter greater than two millimetres at the fifth lumbar or first sacral level indicates abnormal fibrofatty thickening.
steps.tx: **Thickened filum terminale criteria** require an axial T1 MRI diameter exceeding **2.0 mm** measured at the **L5-S1** level. A thick, taut, or fibrolipomatous filum exerts progressive traction on the spinal cord during growth, driving neurological, orthopedic, and urologic dysfunction. Associated fatty infiltration of the filum appears bright on T1 weighted sequences.

steps.say: Spinal dysraphism divides into open and closed varieties. Myelomeningocele exposes the neural placode directly to the environment, uniformly links to Chiari two malformation, and triggers maternal alpha fetoprotein elevation.
steps.tx: Distinguishing **open vs closed dysraphism** rests on skin integrity. Open dysraphism, primarily **myelomeningocele**, exposes neural placode through a posterior spinal defect, universally associates with **Chiari II malformation**, and causes marked elevation of maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein. Closed lesions keep intact skin cover, so raised alpha fetoprotein screening usually stays normal.

points: Skin dimple, hair tuft, or lipoma
right.title: Closed Spinal Dysraphism

steps.say: Subcutaneous lipomas in closed dysraphism attach directly to neural structures. In lipomyelomeningocele, the neural lipoma junction extends through the spina bifida defect into the extraspinal soft tissue.
steps.tx: In **lipomyelocele and lipomyelomeningocele**, a subcutaneous lipomatous mass extends through a dysraphic vertebral defect to attach to the dorsal placode. In lipomyelomeningocele, expansion of the subarachnoid space displaces the **neural-lipoma junction outside the spinal canal**, requiring meticulous reconstructive surgery. Preoperative imaging maps the lipoma placode interface to guide safe untethering and reconstruction.

steps.say: Split cord malformation presents when an osseous or fibrous spur divides the cord into two hemicords. Type one split cords possess separate dural sheaths divided by a rigid bony spur.
steps.tx: **Diastematomyelia and bony spur** malformations present as sagittal division of the spinal cord into two asymmetric hemicords. Type I diastematomyelia features two distinct dural sacs separated by a rigid **osseous or cartilaginous spur**, causing severe progressive neurologic deficits unless surgically resected.

steps.say: A midline cutaneous pit above the natal cleft may represent an epithelial tract penetrating inward. Dermal sinus tracts connect the cutaneous surface directly to the thecal sac, providing a pathway for recurrent bacterial meningitis.
steps.tx: A **dorsal dermal sinus tract** consists of an epithelial tube traversing inward from a cutaneous midline pit located **above the gluteal crease** into the thecal sac. Communication between the external skin flora and the central nervous system creates substantial risk of recurrent chemical or bacterial **meningitis**.

steps.say: Spinal ultrasound represents the first line screening tool for sacral dimples in early infancy. Sound waves easily penetrate through unossified cartilaginous posterior vertebral arches before three to four months of age.
steps.tx: The **neonatal spine ultrasound window** serves as the optimal non-invasive screening tool for midline cutaneous markers in infants under **3-4 months**. Prior to posterior vertebral element ossification, high frequency linear transducers clearly visualize the conus medullaris tip, filum dynamics, and intradural lipomas.

steps.say: Infants of mothers with gestational diabetes face elevated risk for caudal regression syndrome. Radiographs show sacral agenesis and hypoplastic ilia, with the spinal cord tapering bluntly at thoracic levels.
steps.tx: **Caudal regression syndrome** is strongly tied to **maternal gestational diabetes**, resulting in complete or partial **sacral agenesis** with pelvic deformity. Sagittal MRI characteristically shows a distinctive blunt, wedge-shaped conus medullaris ending abnormally high at the **T11-T12** level, with severe motor loss.
